treatment_plan.summary: 67-year-old female with known non-valvular atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc 4) on warfarin (INR 2.4) who has undergone PCI with a drug-eluting stent for NSTEMI, with concurrent Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. This patient requires a carefully balanced antithrombotic strategy managing the dual risk of stent thrombosis and thromboembolism against a significant bleeding risk from triple therapy (VKA + aspirin + clopidogrel).

recommendations.intervention: Initiate Triple Therapy: VKA (Warfarin, target INR 2.0-2.5) + Aspirin 75-100mg daily + Clopidogrel 75mg daily for 3-6 months
recommendations.rationale: For this 67F with AF and NSTEMI post-PCI with DES, triple therapy is recommended in the short term (3-6 months) to balance stent thrombosis risk with bleeding risk.

recommendations.intervention: Step-down to Dual Therapy: VKA (Warfarin, target INR 2.0-3.0) + Clopidogrel 75mg daily (or alternatively aspirin) up to month 12
recommendations.rationale: Following the initial 3-6 months of triple therapy, step down to VKA plus a single antiplatelet to reduce bleeding risk while managing long-term AF and vascular risk.

recommendations.intervention: VKA Monotherapy: Warfarin (target INR 2.0-3.0) after 12 months
recommendations.rationale: For stable vascular disease (>1 year post event) in this AF patient, VKA monotherapy may be considered to prevent long-term stroke risk, as concomitant antiplatelet therapy is generally not recommended without new events.

recommendations.intervention: Dose regulation: Maintain INR at the lower end of the therapeutic range (2.0-2.5) while on combination antiplatelet therapy
recommendations.rationale: To mitigate the high bleeding risk of triple therapy in this 67-year-old, the CPG recommends strict regulation of anticoagulation intensity to the lower target.

recommendations.intervention: Aspirin 300 mg loading dose followed by 75-150 mg daily maintenance
recommendations.rationale: Indicated for the NSTEMI and PCI management; loading and maintenance doses are standard of care for this patient.

recommendations.intervention: Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (following loading dose if not already given)
recommendations.rationale: As part of the antiplatelet strategy post-PCI. It is preferred in combination with VKA after the initial triple therapy period.

recommendations.intervention: Statin therapy — initiate or continue high potency statin (e.g. Atorvastatin 80mg od)
recommendations.rationale: High dose statins are recommended early after admission for UA/NSTEMI to reduce MACE. This patient with T2DM and CAD is at high vascular risk.

recommendations.intervention: Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) — gastric protection
recommendations.rationale: To mitigate the increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding associated with triple antithrombotic therapy in this 67-year-old.

recommendations.intervention: Dietary counseling to reduce calorie-dense food, focus on complex carbohydrates and fruits/vegetables
recommendations.cpg_source: CPG Prevention of CVD in Women §6.1.1 [chunk 17]
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with T2DM and ACS requires lifestyle management for weight and glycemic control as part of comprehensive CV risk reduction.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Cardiology (routine) — St Elevation Myocardial Infarction; trigger: post-STEMI
recommendations.rationale: Early referral for cardiac rehabilitation is advisable.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Physiotherapy (routine) — St Elevation Myocardial Infarction; trigger: post-acute cardiac event
recommendations.rationale: Following an acute cardiac event or post cardiac surgery, patients should be referred to a cardiac rehabilitative physician for exercise prescription.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Multidisciplinary Team (routine) — Atrial Fibrillation
recommendations.rationale: The choice of therapeutic anticoagulation for other indications would depend upon the risk of thrombosis, patients' preference and the consensus of the multidisciplinary team.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Cardiology (urgent) — Atrial Fibrillation; trigger: first occurrence in patients with valvular heart disease
recommendations.rationale: If AF should occur for the first time in patients with valvular heart disease, immediate anticoagulation with UFH is advised.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Cardiology (urgent) — Stemi; trigger: presented initially to non-PCI-capable hospital
recommendations.rationale: STEMI patients who present initially to non-PCI-capable hospitals should be referred for early coronary angiography with a view to revascularization in the presence of any of the following:

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Cardiology (routine) — Unstable Angina / Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction; trigger: post-discharge
recommendations.rationale: referral to a cardiac rehabilitation program where appropriate

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Multidisciplinary Team (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: newly diagnosed
recommendations.rationale: All patients should be referred for formal diabetes education preferably delivered by a multidisciplinary healthcare professional team.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Multidisciplinary Team (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Obesity; trigger: evaluation for bariatric surgery appropriateness
recommendations.rationale: Evaluation for the appropriateness of surgery should be performed by a multidisciplinary team consisting of endocrinologist, bariatric surgeon, psychiatrist, dietitian and physiotherapist prior to surgery.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Multidisciplinary Team (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Adolescents
recommendations.rationale: A multidisciplinary diabetes team is important.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Cardiology (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Abnormal Resting ECG; trigger: abnormal resting ECG at baseline
recommendations.rationale: Baseline resting ECG is recommended. If abnormal, refer to cardiology.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Nephrology (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Diabetic Kidney Disease; trigger: rapid decline in renal function (eGFR loss >5 ml/min/1.73 m² in 1 year or >10 ml/min/1.73 m² in 5 years)
recommendations.rationale: All patients with T2DM and DKD should be referred to a nephrologist in these situations: rapid decline in renal function (eGFR loss >5 ml/min/1.73 m² in 1 year or >10 ml/min/1.73 m² in 5 years)

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Ophthalmology (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: newly diagnosed
recommendations.rationale: Annual dilated eye exam

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Ophthalmology (routine) — Obesity with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: retinopathy with rapid glycaemic improvement on semaglutide
recommendations.rationale: Patients with obesity and T2DM with retinopathy treated with semaglutide should be monitored closely and co-managed with an ophthalmologist.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Ophthalmology (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Obesity and Retinopathy; trigger: baseline retinopathy treated with semaglutide
recommendations.rationale: Patients with obesity and T2DM with retinopathy treated with semaglutide should be monitored closely and co-managed with an ophthalmologist.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Dietetics (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: newly diagnosed
recommendations.rationale: Registered dietitian for medical nutrition therapy

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Psychiatry (consider) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: if indicated
recommendations.rationale: Mental health professional, if indicated

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Dentistry (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: newly diagnosed
recommendations.rationale: Dentist for comprehensive dental and periodontal examination

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Oral Health Professional (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
recommendations.rationale: Therefore, referrals should be done routinely for oral healthcare.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Bariatric Surgery (consider) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: BMI >= 32 kg/m² with inadequate glycaemic control despite lifestyle modification and pharmacotherapy
recommendations.rationale: Bariatric surgery may be considered in patients with BMI ≥32 kg/m² and their T2DM cannot be controlled by lifestyle changes and pharmacotherapy.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Bariatric Surgery (consider) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Obesity; trigger: BMI >= 37.5 kg/m² with inadequately controlled hyperglycaemia despite lifestyle modification and optimal medical treatment
recommendations.rationale: Metabolic surgery should be recommended for Asians with T2DM as below: ≥37.5 kg/m²

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Geriatrics (routine) — Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Cognitive Impairment; trigger: cognitive impairment identified on screening
recommendations.rationale: Annual screening with tools such as the Mini-Mental State Examination, Mini-Cognitive, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the Clinical Frailty Score may help identify patients requiring neuropsychological evaluation and referral to geriatrician.

recommendations.intervention: Refer to Endocrinology (routine) — Diabetes Mellitus; trigger: insulin requirement exceeds 0.1 unit/kg/hour during labour
recommendations.rationale: If requirement exceeds 0.1 unit/kg/hour, refer to the endocrinologist/physician.

red_flags: Signs of major bleeding (hematemesis, melena, intracranial hemorrhage) — stop antithrombotics and seek emergency care
Stent thrombosis symptoms (recurrent acute chest pain, ECG changes) — urgent review for re-catheterization
Severe hypoglycemia or cognitive dysfunction — reassess T2DM regimen and consider de-escalation
follow_up: 1 month: Assess for bleeding complications and check INR stability. Ensure triple therapy is well tolerated.
3-6 months: Re-evaluate for transition from triple therapy to VKA + single antiplatelet (Step-down) if clinically stable.
12 months: Review for step-down to VKA monotherapy if no recurrent ACS or revascularization events.
Ongoing: Annual cognitive and frailty screening given T2DM and age to ensure management aligns with functional status.
unresolved_questions: Specific PPI choice and duration not explicitly detailed in the retrieved chunks, though recommended as 'consider where necessary' in Table 13.
The evidence base strongly notes a 'lack of published evidence' for this specific complex patient profile (AF + NSTEMI + PCI), relying heavily on consensus and balancing risks.
